AuroraCloud to provide sample L3 dataset and expected QPS for bench tests by 2026-05-24
Schedule marketplace listing draft review w/ product & pricing (target 2026-05-28)

summary: Technical sync to align on joint solution reference architecture, marketplace packaging requirements, and bench/QA plan. Focus on VPC onboarding, AMI/container packaging, KMS integration, and a short performance test plan. Agreement on next-steps and owners.
transcript:
Header: 2026-05-19 10:00 PDT | Duration: 56m | Attendees: Ethan Ramos (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Lara Nguyen (AuroraCloud PM), Tomás Alvarez (Aurora Solutions Arch), Jin Park (Aurora Head of Marketplace)

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE on the partner motion; Priya our SE is here. How's everyone?
[00:10] Lara: Hi Ethan, hi Priya, all good. Thanks for setting this up, want to make sure we cover the marketplace packaging and the joint-ref-arch items.
[00:18] Priya: Great, we'll start with a quick run through of the proposed reference architecture then dive into packaging options, AMI vs container, and then KMS and audit/log requirements.
[00:30] Tomás: Sounds good. Quick note, Jin will be focused on the listing/sku parts but Tomás and I will drive the infra details.
[01:02] Priya: Ok, so at a high level — Redwood provides a hosted control plane but for Aurora we propose a private deployment pattern: customer-managed VPC, private control plane peering, and an optional on-prem package for regulated customers. The model serving would run in a dedicated instance pool — we can do dedicated GPU pools or leverage Aurora's marketplace-provisioned instances.
[01:30] Lara: When you say "private control plane peering" — do you mean VPC peering or private link? We need to align with Aurora's governance.
[01:40] Priya: Good question. Either works; we've done AWS PrivateLink and VPC peering. PrivateLink is preferred for stricter network boundaries. We'll note both in the diagram.
[02:15] [Speaker 1/Tomas interjects] Tomás: For marketplace packaging, are you guys packing an AMI we can list or a container with a quick provisioning script? We have different teams that prefer one or the other.
[02:25] Ethan: We can do both. For faster onboarding we often ship a hardened AMI that includes the infra agent + certs pre-provisioned, but many partners prefer a container-based listing (Helm + manifests) for k8s shops.
[02:45] Jin: Our marketplace requires at least two packaging options. Also, listing metadata needs a short blurb and SKU topology.
[02:52] Priya: We'll send a marketplace listing draft — Ethan will follow up with prior joint-solution blurb.
[03:10] [00:03:10] Priya: Now on security — KMS integration is straightforward. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM for on-prem. Audit logs are exported to s3 or to your logging endpoint (we support splunk, datadog ingestion). We'll need Aurora's retention requirements.
[03:35] Lara: SOC2 is a must; we also need an encrypted-in-transit confirmation and documentation for key rotation policies.
[03:42] Priya: Yep, SOC2 and support for SAML/SSO and RBAC are in scope. We'll attach the security whitepaper and a compliance checklist.
[04:05] Tomás: On the networking side — do you do NAT or do you require egress? We prefer minimal egress from our customers' VPCs.
[04:12] Priya: The private control plane model minimizes egress. Only outbound to our control plane endpoints for telemetry; otherwise model inference stays in your VPC. There are options for completely air-gapped on-prem packages.
[04:28] Ethan: For performance, we wanted to align on your expected QPS and latency SLOs so Priya can recommend Dedicated vs Shared-hosted capacity and quantization profiles.
[04:40] Tomás: Initial target is 150 QPS peak for short bursts, steady-state 30 QPS, 95th latency under 120 ms per token if possible — these are rough numbers.
[04:55] Priya: Ok, given that profile we'd recommend dedicated GPU pools with batching enabled and prefix caching; quantized 4-bit models can help keep GPU utilization up. We'll put together a throughput/latency matrix.
[05:20] Lara: And for bench testing — what artifacts do you need from us?
[05:25] Priya: Sample dataset, expected prompt distributions (seq length), and target concurrency. Also test harness access — we can run a perf sweep against a staging pool.
[05:40] Tomás: We'll work on the sample set and get it over by 5/24.
[06:02] Ethan: Great. Marketplace listing specifics — Jin, what are the Aurora requirements for pricing SKUs?
[06:10] Jin: We need: SKU for a one-click deployment (managed), SKU for bring-your-own-license (BYOL) or reserved capacity, and a listing for dedicated-support add-on. Also clear support SLA metadata.
[06:25] Ethan: We'll draft SKU suggestions (consumption vs reserved) and include Redwood pricing bands and support tiers.
[06:33] Priya: A small note about fallback policies — Redwood can expose routing policies so if a customer's dedicated pool is overloaded we can fallback to a compatible hosted variant subject to customer consent; for marketplace listing we need to make that explicit.
[06:50] Lara: We have to be careful about allowed fallbacks in Aurora's marketplace. Sometimes customers balk if data leaves the VPC.
[06:57] Priya: Understood. We'll provide an explicit opt-in parameter in the deployment manifest and document the fallback behavior.
[07:12] Tomás: Ops question: how do you handle KV cache and session state if customers want multi-tenant inference?
[07:20] Priya: KV cache is per-session and we have controls to pin caches to a customer's dedicated pool. It's stored in memory on the inference node; no long-term persistence unless enabled. We also support prefix caching for common prompts to reduce cost.
[07:41] Jin: For the listing we need an explicit paragraph about data residency and retention.
[07:46] Ethan: We'll include a short blurb and link to the compliance docs.
[08:05] Priya: Now for packaging details: AMI path includes pre-baked runtime, kernel-selection heuristics, and an init script that registers the instance with Aurora's market provisioning flow. Container approach uses helm chart + sidecar for the agent and an init job for registering and KMS bootstrap. Both support automatic OS image updates.
[08:30] Lara: Is the init registration interactive or can we do unattended bootstrap? For marketplace one-click we need unattended.
[08:36] Priya: We support unattended via signed bootstrap tokens. We'll provide the token exchange flow in the package checklist.
[08:50] Tomás: Are there any kernel-level dependencies — we run on a broad set of images and need to know if we require specific kernels or GPU drivers.
[08:58] Priya: Drivers: we require NVIDIA drivers for GPU instances (driver versions will be in the checklist). For the AMI we pre-install matching drivers. For containers, we rely on host drivers and recommend the Nvidia container toolkit. We'll include a compatibility matrix.
[09:20] Ethan: Ok moving to bench plan: Priya will run an initial perf sweep with the sample dataset, then we'll do a follow-up with Aurora's staging throughput. Expected deliverables: perf report (latency p50/p95/p99), cost per token estimate, and recommended quantization/profile.
[09:40] Tomás: Timeline?
[09:44] Priya: If we get the sample by 5/24 we can run bench by 5/26 and share a report by 5/29.
[09:52] Lara: That timeline works for us.
[10:05] Jin: For the marketplace listing copy — do you have a marketing blurb template we can adapt?
[10:10] Ethan: Yes, I'll send our prior joint-solution blurb and a short 50-75 word & long 200-300 word versions. Also include screenshots and architecture diagram.
[10:22] Priya: One more technical question: how do we handle secrets/certs in the marketplace deploy flow?
[10:28] Tomás: Specifically for SSO and initial admin user creation, we need an automated flow.
[10:32] Priya: We use KMS-wrapped secrets and provide a bootstrap flow that calls your SSO provider (SAML) for initial admin creation; keys and certs are stored in your KMS. For the AMI we support a one-time encrypt/decrypt step during first boot.
[10:50] Lara: Do you support rotation policies automatically?
[10:54] Priya: Yes, key rotation is supported and we expose hooks for rotation events; we can also integrate with Aurora's central KMS if you prefer.
[11:12] Ethan: Back to compliance — we'll attach SOC2 scoping doc and a compliance checklist. Any additional certs required?
[11:18] Jin: No additional certs right now, but we want to include an optional SOC2 entry in the listing metadata.
[11:25] Priya: Noted. We'll include a compliance badge section.
[11:40] Tomás: For failure modes, can you outline what happens if a dedicated pool is preempted or an instance fails?
[11:48] Priya: Instancing: Redwood has autoscaling and retry policies; for preemption we retry on another instance in the dedicated pool. If the pool cannot satisfy load we surface a capacity alert and, if opted-in, fallback to a hosted compatible model. We'll document RTO and RPO here.
[12:10] Ethan: Ok, quick recap of next steps: Priya will draft the reference architecture and packaging checklist; Ethan will send marketplace copy and previous joint-solution blurb; Tomás to send sample dataset and throughput matrix; Jin to schedule a listing-review meeting for 5/28.
[12:35] Lara: Quick micro-ask — can we get a sample helm values.yaml to validate required params?
[12:40] Priya: Yes, we'll attach a sample values.yaml in the artifact.
[13:00] Tomás: One last question on billing integration — do you expose metering and usage logs we can pull into Aurora's marketplace billing system?
[13:08] Ethan: Yes, Redwood emits per-token and per-request metering to your marketplace via an export endpoint or S3 ingestion. We can map tokens to SKUs. We'll include a sample export schema.
[13:30] Priya: Also note latency/cost tradeoffs — 8-bit/4-bit quantization reduces cost but can affect quality; we'll provide recommended profiles per workload.
[13:50] Jin: Perfect. That should cover it.
[14:02] Ethan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and action items.

Notes/Artifacts referenced:
- Ref arch diagram (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/auroracloud-refarch-v1)
- Marketplace packaging checklist (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/marketplace-packaging-checklist.pdf)
- Security whitepaper & SOC2 summary (link: https://redwood.internal/security/soc2-summary.pdf)
- Prior joint solution blurb (link: https://redwood.app/joint-solutions/redwood-aurora-example)

End of transcript.
